scenario.description: A tenant with an empty room must finalize an informal summer sublet offer to Jordan, deciding the rent, included utilities, deposit, end date, and whether to proceed after hearing from the prospective subtenant, a housemate, and a former roommate.

shared_context.S1: Maya has a furnished room available from June 1 through August 31.
shared_context.S2: Maya decides the final informal sublet offer and whether Jordan gets the room.
shared_context.S3: The room was initially discussed at $850 per month plus the tenant's share of utilities.
shared_context.S4: Maya wants the arrangement's rent, deposit, end date, and reliability expectations settled before June 1.
shared_context.S5: Before finalizing the offer, Maya routinely asks Jordan, Priya, and Eli for anything relevant about the budget and utilities, house rules, and Jordan's reliability, and waits to hear from each of them.

PF1.text: Jordan's fixed summer housing stipend allows Jordan to commit to exactly $900 per month with utilities included, but Jordan cannot commit to more than $900 per month.

PF2.text: The landlord told Priya yesterday that any informal sublet must collect a $300 security deposit and end on August 31; Priya has not shared this with Maya or Jordan yet.

PF3.text: Eli lived with Jordan for eighteen months and can confirm that Jordan paid rent on time every month and left the room in good condition.

acceptance_conditions: The room must be awarded to Jordan.
The monthly rent must be no more than $900.
Utilities must be included in the monthly rent.
The security deposit must be exactly $300.
The sublet must end on August 31.
A reference check with Eli must be completed.
A commitment recording Eli's reliability reference must appear in the settlement.
The housing-stipend constraint must be cited as justification for the final rent and utility arrangement.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'reliability' or c['type'] == 'reliability_commitment' or c['type'] == 'reliability_expectation' or c['type'] == 'reliability_confirmed' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Jordan's exact $900 all-in limit changes the feasible offer from the advertised $850 plus utilities to a bundled arrangement at no more than $900, and supplies the required justification.
The landlord's stated rule changes the settlement to a $300 deposit and an August 31 end date instead of leaving the deposit and termination date open.
Eli's firsthand eighteen-month history changes the settlement from an unverified offer to one that includes a completed reliability reference and a recorded reliability commitment.
